speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if these symptoms happen specifically when you are feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The history of stridor and wheezing exacerbated by feeding, crying, and neck flexion (the sniffing position) is classic for this congenital laryngeal anomaly, compounded by potential gastroesophageal reflux given the vomiting.
